exposure: Gut microbiota composition (Firmicutes phylum, Bifidobacterium concentration)
cohort: The study included 130 infants aged 1-24 months with egg and/or milk allergy and 110 non-food allergic control infants.
finding: The study demonstrated a partial role of TLR4 gene polymorphism (specifically rs4986790 and rs4986791) and gut microbiota (increased Firmicutes phylum and Bifidobacterium concentration) in the development of food allergies.
